short: In a PLINK fileset, a person whose father and mother IDs (columns 3 and 4 of the .fam file) are both 0, meaning unknown. PLINK computes allele frequencies, Hardy–Weinberg tests and LD from founders only.
long:
A person with a father or mother ID filled in is a nonfounder, even if that parent is not in the fileset. --make-founders clears parent IDs that point to people who are absent, so those people count as founders, and --nonfounders makes --freq, --maf, --hardy and --hwe count everyone. Counting founders only keeps alleles that relatives share by descent from being counted more than once, which would bias allele frequencies and the Hardy–Weinberg test.

In a study of unrelated people every person is a founder: PennCATH's log reports 1,401 founders and 0 nonfounders.
l1: Page 16 (QC step 2): --hardy and --hwe count founders only. Page 17 (QC step 3): --indep-pairwise computes r² in founders.

short: For a test on counts: the probability of every outcome less likely than the one observed, plus half the probability of the outcomes exactly as likely. It is always a little smaller than the ordinary exact p-value.
long:
An exact test on counts, such as the Hardy–Weinberg exact test, can produce only a limited set of p-values. The ordinary exact p-value counts the observed outcome in full, so under the null hypothesis it falls below a level such as 0.05 less often than 5% of the time: the test is conservative. Counting the outcomes tied with the observed one at half weight brings the rate closer to the nominal level (Graffelman and Moreno 2013).

PLINK 1.9 computes it with the midp modifier of --hardy and --hwe, and its documentation recommends it. A SNP with only one allele has a single possible outcome, so its exact p-value is 1 and its mid-p value 0.5.
l1: Page 16 (QC step 2): the widget shows both p-values, and the example filter is --hwe 1e-6 midp.

links.t: Graffelman & Moreno 2013, The mid p-value in exact tests for Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
